# Draft:Edinburgh Fringe First Awards

The Scotsman Fringe First Awards, often called the Fringe Firsts, are theatre awards presented by The Scotsman for new writing premiered at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. Established in 1973, the awards are presented in several rounds across the festival rather than as a single annual prize.
History
The awards were established in 1973 by Scotsman arts editor Allen Wright and Edinburgh Festival Fringe administrator John Milligan to recognise new writing at the Fringe.
Format and eligibility
Eligible shows must be listed in the theatre, dance and physical theatre, musicals and opera, or children's shows sections of the Fringe programme. Cabaret shows may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
Productions must run for at least eight days. The work must be dramatic in form with a substantial narrative or character-based element; abstract dance and movement pieces are not eligible. The awards are intended for work premiered in Edinburgh rather than productions already widely reviewed or staged elsewhere.
Sponsorship
In 2024 the awards were jointly sponsored by Edinburgh Napier University and Queen Margaret University. In 2025 they were sponsored by Queen Margaret University and Stagecoach.
